subject: Helix Labs MAP: close safeguard & re-baseline proposal
messages:
From: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helixlabs.com
Date: 2024-02-28T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP & eval timeline — risk to 3/22 go-live

Tessa,

Thanks for the call earlier. I wanted to put the current state in writing: our security team just pushed the SOC2 evidence collection window by two weeks (vendor side delay), which directly impacts the acceptance gate in our MAP. At this point I'm worried the go-live we discussed (Mar 22) is at risk unless we rework the evaluation plan or accept a phased go-live.

Key constraints: procurement can only sign once legal finalizes the data processing addendum (DPA) — legal now needs additional logs that we didn't account for. Procurement has also flagged an internal approval meeting on Mar 8 that could push things further.

Can Redwood propose either a compressed evaluation plan with a canary fallback, or a re-baseline that keeps our internal milestones but shifts customer-facing launch? We need this by EOD Monday so I can update my execs.

Sally
Sally Park
Head of IT, Helix Labs
attachments: Helix_procurement_timeline.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2024-02-28T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline — risk to 3/22 go-live

Sally — thanks for the heads-up and for the timeline PDF.

Quick proposals while we triage with your legal/procurement:
- Option 1 (Phased go-live): keep a scoped beta for an internal team on Mar 22 (minimal data surface) and expand to full customer launch after SOC2 evidence is cleared.
- Option 2 (Compressed eval + canary): compress acceptance tests to high-priority scenarios (list below), run a 1-week canary window immediately after procurement sign, aim full launch by Apr 12.
- Option 3 (Re-baseline): shift MAP milestones by two full weeks; put a firm internal cutover on Apr 5 with customer-facing launch Apr 19.

I'll pull Marcus into cadence/discount conversations and Laura for the acceptance gating changes. We can run a 30-min triage call tomorrow; what times work for you?

Deliverable: Redwood will share a proposed MAP variant with milestone dates and a contingency runbook by Mar 3 COB.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2024-03-01T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline — risk to 3/22 go-live

Thanks, Sally & Tessa. I mapped three pragmatic paths and the commercial/ops implications:

1) Scoped beta (keeps 3/22 milestone): limited feature set, Redwood provides 30% usage credit for first month if go-live is limited by SOC2 acceptance. No change to contract language.

2) Compressed eval + canary (preferred): compress acceptance to top 6 test cases, Redwood runs the canary with a dedicated SE (Laura) for three weeks. We can offer a one-time implementation credit equal to 10% of first month fees if Helix accepts the canary route.

3) Formal re-baseline: push customer launch by 3 weeks; Redwood will not charge for the canary environment for the interim period. Procurement/legal give us dates and we supply an updated SOW + milestone-based invoice schedule.

I attached a proposed MAP worksheet (Helix_MAP_v3.xlsx) that aligns milestones with owner and required artifacts. Laura — can you confirm acceptance test reduction and whether any additional infra work is needed for the canary?

—Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
attachments: Helix_MAP_v3.xlsx

From: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helixlabs.com, legal@helixlabs.com
Date: 2024-03-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline — risk to 3/22 go-live

Marcus — thank you, this is helpful. Procurement confirms they can move their internal approval to Mar 8 if we get a signed DPA routing by Mar 4. Legal asked that Redwood provide a short appendix describing our log retention and redaction controls (they called it "DPA addendum A").

We prefer Option 2 (Compressed eval + canary) but need the following guarantees to present to our execs: 
- A concrete list of acceptance tests that will be dropped vs. retained (so we can risk-rate them).
- An explicit rollback plan if canary shows data leakage or latency > 300ms for production queries.
- Confirmation of the 10% implementation credit and the duration of the canary environment.

I'll attach an updated procurement timeline (Helix_procurement_timeline.pdf). If you can get the appendix + updated MAP and SOW by Mar 3 COB, procurement will commit to the Mar 8 approval meeting.

Thanks,
Sally

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2024-03-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline — risk to 3/22 go-live

On Mar 1, Sally Park wrote:
> Marcus — thank you, this is helpful. Procurement confirms they can move their internal approval to Mar 8 if we get a signed DPA routing by Mar 4.

Sally — technical confirmations below (short form):
- Acceptance test reduction: we'll retain the top 6 API/latency functional tests and the full security checklist for data handling; non-essential UX flows (bulk import UI edge cases) will be deferred to post-launch. Detail in attached SOC2_evidence_request.pdf.
- Rollback plan: immediate traffic reroute to a read-only snapshot and feature-flag shutoff that we can execute within 15 minutes; we'll provide runbook and on-call escalation matrix during the canary.
- Canary duration & infra: propose a 2-week canary with a dedicated SE and daily health digests. Redwood will host the canary in a segmented environment (no customer PII), and maintain KV cache isolation.

I'll coordinate with Marcus on the SOW language for the rollback SLA and with Tessa for the acceptance checklist in the MAP.

Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: SOC2_evidence_request.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@helixlabs.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@helixlabs.com, legal@helixlabs.com
Date: 2024-03-04T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Decision & next steps — compressed eval + canary (MAP v3)

Team — aligned summary and commitments:

Decision: Helix & Redwood agree to Option 2: compressed evaluation + 2-week canary.

Commitments (Redwood):
- Deliver updated MAP worksheet (Helix_MAP_v3.xlsx) with acceptance checklist and redlines by 2024-03-03 COB — DONE (shared link).
- Deliver DPA Addendum A (log retention & redaction summary) by 2024-03-03 COB — in progress; legal looped.
- Provide canary environment for 2 weeks starting immediately after procurement sign-off; dedicated SE support (Laura) and daily health digest.
- Commercial concession: 10% implementation credit on month 1 invoice if canary is accepted and full launch follows.

Contingency runbook highlights:
- If canary shows data leakage or latency above 300ms sustained for >10 mins, Redwood will pause traffic and execute rollback runbook (15-minute target to cut).
- If procurement cannot approve on Mar 8, stakeholder will escalate to execs and we will revert to formal re-baseline (target launch Apr 19).

Next steps for Helix: confirm procurement will target Mar 8 after reviewing DPA addendum. Please reply-all with a single-line acceptance ("Helix accepts compressed eval + canary") so we can lock dates and issue SOW amendment.

Thanks — appreciate the collaborative run to keep momentum.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference
attachments: Helix_MAP_v3.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_request.pdf
links: https://drive.redwood.com/HLX/Map_v3, HubSpot: HLX-1234
